parsed.explanation: Documented as a lever against trans people, not a dead letter: Article 489 carries 6 months-3 years, 170 charges in 2018, wide police discretion, and a Jan 2026 report that it is used to arrest trans people for gender expression, plus Article 498 moral charges. Police targeting, public naming, filming/ID posting in 2019 and forced genital display alleged in 2024 show state outing and predation. Official hostility (justice minister 'trash', religious authority opposing transition, blocked organisations, school curriculum), no anti-discrimination recourse, and a 2020 outing campaign with evictions show societal hostility with no remedy. If outed, a visitor faces arrest, public exposure, prolonged detention/prosecution on thin evidence and significant violence/harassment risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Police photograph and post identity documents after appearance-based stops; no visitor document procedure recorded. Documented police targeting of perceived LGBTQ people.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch or visibility at police stop can trigger Article 489/498 investigation and involuntary outing.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arrest for gender expression under Articles 489/498, arbitrary arrests, handcuffing, forced genital display alleged 2024, public naming before trial, sentences 6 months-3 years documented for same-sex conduct.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No effective complaint/discipline route documented; organisations blocked.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Investigation becomes custody exposure; thin-evidence prosecutions and publicised names increase violence and detention risk. Custody placement by sex not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom/facility access rule for visitors; public outing in streets and by police documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of documented facility ban does not offset police stops and public exposure in shared spaces.

care_services.exposure: No gender-affirming healthcare framework, self-medication reported, de facto prohibition on surgery for citizens; no current visitor access recorded.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or continuing care if outed is unresolved; medication interruption risk without documented visitor protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Justice minister called homosexuals 'trash', senior religious authority opposes transition, curriculum frames 'unnatural acts' as danger/depravity, authorities block LGBTIQ organisations, police disproportionately target perceived LGBTQ.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses police enforcement and social hostility, making outing more consequential.

minors_guardians.exposure: 2020 campaign pressured young people's family ties; no age-specific visitor rule documented. Accompanying minor does not mitigate adult arrest/outing exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: If guardian arrested or outed, family separation and public exposure risks follow; no documented shelter provision for visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Public identification carries significant risk of violence/harassment; 2020 outing campaign, evictions, alleged suicide; 2022 trans woman beaten; marches demanding punishment after 2007 convictions; only 21% acceptance in 2018-19 survey.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2022 assault led to arrests of 3 minors and an adult — isolated prosecution; no pattern of protection documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police as perpetrators in 2019/2024 undermine recourse for street violence; social hostility escalates after state outing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination/harassment law, no legal gender recognition pathway (resident gap noted but visitor documents from home still lead to outing), prosecutions on thin evidence, no published current prosecution figures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns on custody placement and healthcare do not resolve toward safety; documented enforcement and lack of recourse dominate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: appearance-based police detention, custody humiliation, officials framing trans people negatively, legal aid only occasional relief. This case has longer statutory sentences (up to 3 years) and forced genital display, so at or slightly below 0.25.

Lower than 0.15-E: no documented pattern of birth-sex cell sexual assault, guesthouse raids or weeks-long detention; arrests are documented but custody sexual violence rate is not established. The case is therefore above the severe tier, but far below reduced risk.

Higher risk than 0.35-C: 0.35-C involves stops/extortion usually ending in release after payment. Here charges lead to imprisonment, public naming/posting, and no documented complaint mechanism that secures release or refunds.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is hostile at every stage: visibility triggers police stops, document filming and genital inspection; Articles 489/498 convert gender expression into arrest with 6-month to 3-year exposure; public naming and a 2020 outing campaign amplify street violence and eviction; official/religious framing and blocked organisations leave no recourse. Isolated arrests after a 2022 beating do not offset police-perpetrated outing. Custody placement and visitor healthcare are undocumented, not safe. A visitor who is outed faces likely detention and prosecution, placing this in high risk near the severe threshold.
